why: Fixture tests_m6/fixtures/i123/sol/Pre05.sol amended. Instrument defect found while building, before any measured run: solc 0.5.17 writes inline assembly as text, with no Yul AST, so the Solidity frontend refuses the whole Pre05 document at extraction ('inline assembly ... has no Yul AST (this compiler writes assembly as text): the walker cannot read it'), and P2 could not hold under any implementation of the typed model. Pre05's one assembly function (sarYC, a Yul sar by 260) is removed; Pre06 and Pre07 keep theirs (0.6.12 and 0.7.6 give a Yul AST), and SortOps keeps the Yul forms under 0.8.24. Pre05's other functions, every other fixture, every claim and every expected value are unchanged; the harness's Pre05 cases drop sarYC accordingly.

Fixture tests_m6/fixtures/i123/sol/SortOps.sol amended. Instrument defect found while building, before any measured run: the in-class contract SortOps held uncheckedSubT (unchecked last - block.timestamp - block.timestamp). The sort pass (holon sorts, unchanged) reads that whole term as a signed difference SDur with a sign obligation, a SORT realize site whose law states the sign of the unbounded difference. Under W1 the outer ill-sorted SDur - Time is a word, and stating the site from that word would conclude a sign (a sort fact) from a word-level result, which the key's own rule forbids; so the model generator refuses the site, and with it the whole SortOps document, under any implementation of the key. The function moves to a new contract RSignSite in the same file, which stays refused (it is reported, not predicted); SortOps keeps uncheckedT (Time + Time, unchecked, no sign site). The harness's cases drop uncheckedSubT. No claim or expected value changes; P1's case count stays above its floor.

Instrument defect found while building, before any measured run: the check built a section over Pre05's typed model without the opt-in, but without the opt-in Pre05's model is refused (its sarC is a sar, outside the language before I123, as P6 itself predicts), so no section can be built over it and the check could hold under no implementation. It now uses PreVar05 (the same file and release, whose model builds without the opt-in). The claim (without the opt-in a section still refuses a constant shift the model does not define) and the asserted message are unchanged.
